what: Western Midstream gathers, processes and transports natural gas, crude oil and produced water, mostly in the Delaware basin and the Rockies. Occidental Petroleum is its largest customer and controlling holder.
customers: Oil and gas producers, principally Occidental Petroleum, plus third-party producers in its basins.
money: gas gathering, processing and crude and water gathering
pipeline transport of gas and liquids
moat: Gathering systems physically connected to wells under long-term contracts with minimum volume commitments, which cannot be bypassed once laid.
risks: Debt of about $9 billion against almost no cash
Occidental controls it and is also its biggest customer, which limits minority influence
Volumes depend on Delaware basin drilling activity
It is a partnership, which complicates tax reporting for some investors
opportunities: A distribution yield around 9% backed by fee-based contracts
Operating margin of 42% with a 31% net margin
Produced water handling grows with every new Permian well drilled
